task1_bert_tag_classifier.note: Below the illustrative benchmark (~0.48) due to weaker pseudo-text signal vs real captions -- a documented, deliberate tradeoff. Model shows an under-prediction pattern (conservative at 0.5 threshold) rather than over-prediction.

task2_gnn_cnn_comparison.note: CNN substantially outperforms GNN. Attributed to the GNN's coarse node features (5-6 nodes/graph, 5s-averaged chroma) vs the CNN's full-resolution spectrogram input, not a bug -- both trained/evaluated on the identical split for a fair comparison.

task3_gnn_bert_fusion.note: GNN-only collapses to predicting zero positive tags for every clip (confirmed via diagnostic, not a bug) -- chroma features carry no usable signal for caption-derived semantic/mood/quality tags, unlike Task 2's genre task. BERT-only slightly outperforms full fusion on this metric, an honestly-reported finding. Cross-attention weights are near-uniform even after masking padding, likely due to limited training data (~927 examples) for a 110M-parameter attention mechanism.

task4_contrastive_retrieval.note: Retrieval recall is meaningfully above chance in both directions, confirming real learned cross-modal alignment. Zero-shot tagging is far below Task 3's supervised result -- contrastive pretraining alone learns weak alignment; explicit supervision is far more effective for the tagging task.
